subject: mathematics
title: Capacity Lab
objective: Measure capacity in liters or milliliters with an appropriate tool.
introduction: Milo fills his water bottle! 💧 Capacity tells how much a container can hold — small amounts in milliliters, big amounts in liters.

vocabulary.definition: A small water bottle holds only a little, so its capacity is in milliliters.
A big bucket holds a lot, so its capacity is in liters.
A measuring cup shows small amounts in milliliters.

items.prompt: A small water bottle holds a little water. Which unit should you use to measure its capacity?
items.explanation: Milliliters measure small amounts of liquid, and a water bottle holds a small amount. Grams, degrees, and centimeters measure weight, heat, and length.

items.prompt: Milo fills a big bucket with water for the plants. Which unit measures its capacity?
items.explanation: A bucket holds a large amount of water, and liters measure large amounts. Milliliters are only for small containers.

items.prompt: Milo pours juice into a measuring cup. Which unit is best for the small amount?
items.explanation: A measuring cup holds a small amount, so milliliters is the right unit. Liters are for much bigger containers like buckets.

items.prompt: A jerry can holds a lot of water for the trip. Which unit measures its capacity?
items.explanation: A jerry can holds a large amount, so its capacity is measured in liters. Milliliters would only suit a tiny container.

items.prompt: Which unit tells how much liquid a small bottle can hold?
items.explanation: Milliliters measure small amounts of liquid, so they are right for a small bottle’s capacity.
